name: Shapiro delay: radial null coordinate travel time between fixed areal radii in Schwarzschild, dt = (R2 - R1) + 2M ln((R2 - 2M)/(R1 - 2M)); and the weak-field one-way form 2M ln[(x1+r1)/(x0+r0)] (Shapiro 1964)

source.located: Shapiro, I. I., 'Fourth Test of General Relativity', Phys. Rev. Lett. 13, 789 (1964) -- pre-arXiv, no copy on alphaXiv. Restated exactly in: Will, 'The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment', Living Rev. Relativ. 17, 4 (2014), arXiv:1403.7377, Sec. 4.1.2 eqs. (62)-(63) [READ]; Possel, 'The Shapiro time delay and the equivalence principle', arXiv:2001.00229 (2019/2020), eqs. (17), (19), (21), (25), (27) and Sec. IV history [READ]; del Barco, 'Picosecond-level corrections to the Shapiro time delay in a Schwarzschild spacetime', arXiv:2509.11366 (2025), eqs. (2.1)-(2.7), (2.11)-(2.12) [READ]. IAU 2015 Resolution B3, arXiv:1510.07674 [READ] for the solar datum.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1403.7377, 2001.00229, 2509.11366, 1510.07674; discover_papers once. The 1964 PRL itself is NAMED-NOT-READ: its formula, coordinates (Schwarzschild, per Possel Sec. IV: 'Shapiro's first derivation is based on Schwarzschild coordinates, while the formulae he later used to fit his observational results are those based on isotropic coordinates') and year are taken from the restatements.

published_statement: Will 2014 eq. (62), round trip, PPN: delta_t = 2(1+gamma) M_sun ln[ (r_earth + x_earth.n)(r_e - x_e.n) / d^2 ], with eq. (63) for a grazing ray delta_t ~ (1+gamma)/2 [240 - 20 ln(d^2/r)] us. Possel 2020 eq. (27), one way, GR: Delta_t = (2GM/c^3) ln[(x_E + r_E)/(x_P + r_P)] = (2GM/c^3) ln[(r_E + n.x_E)(r_P - n.x_P)/eta^2], derived (eq. 25) from the isotropic-coordinate Schwarzschild metric on a straight line to first order in GM/(c^2 r); in Schwarzschild coordinates the same first-order straight-line calculation carries an extra -GM eta^2/(c^2 r^3) term (eq. 21) and 'comparison with the post-Newtonian expansion shows that the derivation based on isotropic coordinates is correct'. del Barco 2025 eq. (2.1): the exact Schwarzschild coordinate-time law c dt/dr = (1 - r_s/r)^-1 [1 - (1 - r_s/r) b^2/r^2]^-1/2, whose b = 0 (radial) case integrates to the tree's closed form. 'In the two decades following Irwin Shapiro's 1964 discovery of this effect as a theoretical consequence of GR, several high-precision measurements were made'; Cassini 2003: gamma - 1 = (2.1 +- 2.3) x 10^-5 (Will Sec. 4.1.2).
published_hypotheses: Static, spherically symmetric vacuum exterior (Schwarzschild) of a single body of mass M > 0; the Sun in the 1964 setting (Will Sec. 4.1.2; del Barco Sec. 4: 'can only be applied to astrophysical situations where the central massive body is spherical and static')
Weak field, first order in GM/(c^2 r), for the logarithmic formula (Possel eqs. 15-16, 25; Will eq. 62 is PPN, i.e. first post-Newtonian)
Straight (undeflected) coordinate path between emitter and receiver for the first-order formula (Possel Sec. III: 'We have approximated the trajectory of the light as a straight line')

Coordinate (PPN / isotropic / harmonic) time and coordinate positions: the delay is 'the coordinate time delay Delta t, which is not the time an Earth-based clock would measure' (del Barco Sec. 2.1, eq. 2.5 gives the proper-time correction factor (1 + 3 r_s/(4 r_E)) for an Earth clock)

The chart matters at first order: the isotropic (PN) form is the one that matches the post-Newtonian expansion and observation; the Schwarzschild-chart straight-line form differs by a term -GM eta^2/(c^2 r^3) (Possel eqs. 21, 25; del Barco eqs. 2.6 vs 2.11)

Round trip = 2 x one way (Possel Sec. III: 'the additional delay amounts to twice the value for one-way travel'); Will's eq. 62 is the round-trip form with 2(1+gamma), Possel's eq. 27 the one-way GR form with 2GM/c^3
Coefficient (1+gamma)/2 = 1 in GR; it is the measured parameter, not an assumption, since 1968 (Will Sec. 4.1.2)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (tree, foliation.py:568-574): the exact radial form dt = (R2-R1) + 2M ln((R2-2M)/(R1-2M)) is NOT the 1964 formula. Shapiro 1964 is first order, non-radial, Schwarzschild-chart (Possel Sec. IV); the tree's closed form is the b = 0 exact integral of del Barco eq. (2.1). Attribution discrepancy only: at foliation's numbers (R1 = 10M) the 1964-style first-order 2M ln(R2/R1) = 4.605 M is 8.1 % below the exact 5.011 M, so foliation is right to use the exact form and should not call it Shapiro's; the effect is the same.

IMPLICIT, not dropped (foliation.py:308-313 '5.6 % DELAY'; :571 excess = dt - (R2 - R1)): the excess is measured against the AREAL GAP in KILLING time. Against the proper radial distance (92.452 M, computed here) the excess is 2.559 M = 2.8 %; the far static clock (94.056 M) also exceeds it, but the NEAR static clock at 10M reads 84.980 M for the same interval, LESS than 92.452 M. 'DELAY' is therefore the Killing-time / asymptotic-clock statement, which is exactly Shapiro's and Gao-Wald's; foliation labels the number 'Killing time' so the hypothesis is stated, but the percentage is baseline-relative and the file does not say so.

IMPLICIT (foliation.py:569-570 'the mouths are worldlines'): the worldlines are STATIC (Killing) observers at fixed areal radius; 'proper time at the far mouth' :309 is a static observer's dtau = sqrt(1-2M/R2) dt. A free-falling mouth would read differently. Not a fault -- the tree's D4 is defined on static mouths -- but the word 'static' does not appear at the site.

BOUNDARY (foliation.py:314-316): 'Gao & Wald and Visser-Bassett-Liberati say the sign of that excess is forced by the NEC and does not depend on staticity' -- that is a different external result (Gao-Wald 2000), not Shapiro's; Shapiro's formula is static Schwarzschild only. Out of scope here; audited under its own key.

ADDED domain (composite.py:28-29, 64; concentric.py:5-7 'the Shapiro delay, being linear, flips sign' under M -> -M): the source states the formula for M > 0 (the Sun). The extension to M < 0 is the tree's. It holds: the first-order form is odd in M, and the exact radial form 2M ln((R2-2M)/(R1-2M)) is negative for every M < 0, 0 < R1 < R2 (z3, no counterexample). The physical admissibility of M < 0 is composite/concentric's own hypothesis (positive mass theorem), not Shapiro's.

UNNAMED in composite.py (:270-272 delay = dt - |dx|): a first-order 't - |dx|' is chart-dependent at O(2M) -- the Schwarzschild-chart straight-line extra term -M(x1/r1 - x0/r0) evaluates to -4.0e-3 at composite's defaults against the isotropic value 4.415e-2 (9.1 %). composite's metric (:35, isotropic linearised) and chord are consistently isotropic, and Possel/del Barco say that chart is the PN-correct one, so the 0.6 % validation is against the matching formula. Recorded because composite.py:45-46 calls it 'the analytic Shapiro' without naming the chart the analytic form is only valid in.

NONE (composite.py:284-287 analytic_shapiro): one-way 2M ln[(x1+r1)/(x0+r0)] is Possel eq. (27) with GM/c^3 -> M, and Will eq. (62) one-way at gamma = 1. Hypotheses 'straight path' and 'first order in M' are carried and are what VALIDATION 3's symmetric residue (path lengthening ~M^2) explicitly separates.

NAMES-NOT-READS (concentric.py:149-151): concentric inherits composite's validation; nothing in concentric rests on Shapiro beyond linearity in M. Its interior-only lead is withdrawn by the owner (:34-35) and lead_is_global() is asserted False; that withdrawal is concentric's own measurement (convergence with M_ADM = 0), not a Shapiro-formula claim.

A.15) from the same null ODE (eq. 2.1) whose radial limit is foliation's closed form; first-order Schwarzschild-chart formula off by ~400 ps at solar grazing, second order sub-ps; the two 1PN forms in the literature (Misner eq. 2.11 vs Malta eq. 2.12) differ by up to 39.31 us at r0 = 1 R_sun -- a discrepancy inside the first-order literature about a square-root term, which does not touch the radial or the isotropic-log form the tree uses. lacked_data: What Shapiro had in 1964: the Schwarzschild metric, the AU from 1961-64 planetary radar (GM_sun/c^3 to ~1e-5), and radar timing to Venus/Mercury at the ~10 us level. What came later: the measurements themselves (1968, 1971, Viking 1976 at 0.1 %, Cassini 2003 at 2.3e-5 on gamma), the PPN framework that made the coefficient a parameter (1968-72), the resolution of the first-order chart ambiguity (isotropic/harmonic is the PN-correct chart; Possel 2020 Sec. IV), the exact elliptic-integral form and its second-order expansion (del Barco 2025: <= 400 ps against ~300 us), and pulsar Shapiro delays in strong-field binaries. Does having it change the conclusion? No, and the evidence runs the other way on every axis: the coefficient is measured at (1+gamma)/2 = 1 to 1.2e-5; the exact form differs from first order by ~2e-6 of the effect in the solar system; the sign is a delay on the whole Schwarzschild domain (z3). For the tree's own use nothing was lacked at all: foliation.py integrates the exact null ODE with M = 1 and no datum, and composite.py measures against the first-order isotropic form at M/b = 6.7e-3 where the neglected second order is what its symmetric residue isolates. The one thing later work did change is bookkeeping: Shapiro's 1964 chart (Schwarzschild) was not the chart his 1971 fits used, and a first-order 't - |dx|' is chart-dependent at O(2M) -- a limitation, named here, that the tree's isotropic-consistent pipeline does not fall into.
grade_evidence: Statement as used: foliation's exact radial closed form is the b = 0 integral of the Schwarzschild null ODE (sympy residual 0; pins to 1e-11; live selftest OK); composite's analytic_shapiro is Possel eq. (27) / Will eq. (62) one-way at gamma = 1 verbatim (sympy residual 0 at the defaults; VALIDATION 3 reproduces at 1.0061 from the pins and 1.00608 live). Hypotheses as used: Schwarzschild, static mouths, Killing time, isotropic chart, weak field at composite's numbers -- each present in the source and none dropped; two are implicit rather than stated (areal-gap baseline and static-observer clock, both measured here and both leaving the sign intact: 95.011 > 92.452 on the proper-distance baseline). Sign: positive for all M > 0, 2M < R1 < R2 (z3, unsat on the negation, domain non-empty), and the tree's added M < 0 sign flip also holds. Data: no datum enters the tree's use (M = 1); the solar datum and gamma have moved by < 1e-5 and 2e-5 respectively and confirm rather than move the 1964 conclusion. No later paper read here contradicts; the 39 us Misner/Malta 1PN discrepancy (del Barco) is inside a non-radial square-root term the tree does not use. Discrepancies recorded, none repaired: (i) the key attributes to 'Shapiro 1964' an exact radial form Shapiro did not publish -- a naming discrepancy, not a refutation; (ii) '5.6 % DELAY' is 2.8 % on the proper-distance baseline and the near static clock reads less than the proper distance -- the Killing-time statement is the one Shapiro and Gao-Wald make and the one foliation labels, so this is a named hypothesis, not a fault.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if any owner is found to quote the 5.6 % or the 'DELAY' as clock-independent or as holding for a free-falling or near-mouth observer (specthm.py:824 and :2203 quote '%.3f M Shapiro DELAY' in M units, i.e. the Killing-time excess, so they do not); or if composite's delay were ever compared against the Schwarzschild-chart first-order form (its 9.1 % chart term would then masquerade as physics). WRONG only on a shown counterexample to the sign on the stated domain, which z3 excludes over the reals, or a sympy residual != 0, which it is not. DATA-DEPENDENT cannot apply while the tree's use is dimensionless (M = 1). OPEN if the 1964 PRL, once read, states hypotheses the three restatements omit; reading it is the one outstanding act, and it can only add a hypothesis, not remove the integral.
